title: Chemical short-range order increases the phonon heat conductivity in a refractory high-entropy alloy

recollection.starting_material: A refractory high‐entropy alloy composed of multiple refractory elements (for example, species like Mo, Nb, Ta, W, etc.) in a nominally random solid solution.
recollection.intervention: A thermal/processing treatment designed to induce chemical short-range order (CSRO) within the alloy, possibly combined with experimental techniques (such as annealing) and atomistic simulations to track ordering.
recollection.structure: The formation of nanoscale domains where atoms preferentially occupy certain sites, leading to short-range ordered clusters embedded in an overall disordered matrix.
recollection.mechanism: The presence of CSRO reduces the local lattice distortion and thereby lowers the rate of phonon scattering. This leads to an increase in the phonon mean free path, enhancing the overall thermal (phonon) conductivity in the alloy.
recollection.results: A significant enhancement in phonon heat conductivity was observed, with quantitative improvements estimated around 30–50% compared to the fully random alloy; these results were supported by both experimental thermal measurements and computational modeling.

score.note: The recollection generically identifies induced chemical short-range order but incorrectly suggests thermal annealing/experiments rather than varying SRO through Monte Carlo simulation. It recognizes nanoscale ordered clusters but misses the specific HfTi/TiZr, B2-like, percolating structures. The reduced-lattice-distortion and reduced-phonon-scattering mechanism is correct, though the percolation pathways and phonon-DOS changes are omitted. The claimed 30–50% increase is far from the actual ~12%.
